checklists.title: Before responding to a suspicious message
checklists.when_to_use: A message asks you to click a link, act urgently, share information, or make a payment.
steps: Pause. Urgent language is a reason to verify, not a reason to act faster.
Do not share a password, one-time code, PIN, CVV, or identity document in response to an unexpected message.
Do not use links or phone numbers provided in the message.
Open the official app or website yourself, or call a number printed on your card or official documents.
If the request is unexpected, confirm it with the organization using a separate trusted channel.

checklists.title: When you receive a UPI collect request
checklists.when_to_use: Someone says you must approve a payment request or enter your UPI PIN to receive money or a refund.
steps: Read the request in your payment app before taking any action.
Remember that entering a UPI PIN authorizes a payment; it is not required to receive money.
Decline unexpected collect requests and do not scan a QR code to receive a refund.
Verify refunds with the merchant or organization through its official app or contact details.
If you approved a payment you did not intend to make, contact your bank or payment provider promptly.

checklists.title: If you sent money to a suspected scammer
checklists.when_to_use: You made a transfer or payment and think it may have gone to a scammer.
steps: In India, call the cyber fraud helpline at 1930 as soon as possible.
Contact your bank or payment provider using its official app or a trusted phone number. Ask them to report and review the transaction.
Report the incident at cybercrime.gov.in.
Save transaction references, messages, phone numbers, and screenshots.
Change any PIN or password you shared, and secure any affected accounts.

checklists.title: If you shared a password or account details
checklists.when_to_use: You entered credentials or shared a one-time code, PIN, card details, or identity information.
steps: Use the official app or website to change affected passwords and PINs.
If the service offers it, sign out other sessions and review recent account activity.
Contact the bank or service provider through its official channel if payment or identity details were exposed.
Do not share additional codes with anyone who contacts you, even if they claim to be helping.
Keep a record of what was shared and when.

checklists.title: If someone asked for remote access
checklists.when_to_use: A caller or message asks you to install a screen-sharing or remote-control app.
steps: Do not install the app or share your screen with an unexpected caller.
If you already granted access, disconnect the session and remove the remote-access app when it is safe to do so.
Contact your bank using a different trusted device if payment information may have been visible.
Change exposed passwords from a device you trust and review recent account activity.
Get technical support through the device maker's or service provider's official website.

checklists.title: When reviewing suspicious email headers
checklists.when_to_use: You are checking the sender, reply address, or routing details of an email.
steps: Compare the From and Reply-To addresses and look carefully for misspelled or lookalike domains.
Review SPF, DKIM, and DMARC results when available, but do not treat a displayed result alone as proof that an email is genuine.
Remember that headers can be incomplete or forged, and parsed evidence may not have been independently verified.
Treat links and attachments as untrusted until you verify them through a separate official channel.
Do not infer a person's identity or intent from a server location alone.

checklists.title: When an offer asks for an upfront fee
checklists.when_to_use: A prize, job, loan, refund, or other opportunity requires a fee before you receive it.
steps: Be cautious of unexpected offers that require payment to release money or begin work.
Do not send money, gift cards, cryptocurrency, or payment credentials to claim an unsolicited offer.
Verify the organization through contact information you find independently.
Do not share identity documents or banking details until you have confirmed the organization and purpose.
Keep the message and payment request as evidence if you need to report it.
